adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's Turkey country overview supplies the national framework a visitor to an interior province like Düzce stands under: consensual same-sex activity has been decriminalised since the 1858 Ottoman penal code, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, but Turkish marriage law still gives same-sex relationships no legal recognition and offers no civil unions, domestic partnerships or joint adoption, while no comprehensive law bans discrimination on sexual orientation or gender identity and LGBTQ people are barred from open military service. It also tracks the criminalisation push the record's HRW source describes: in early 2026 Turkish media reported the government was considering legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex', and that provision was ultimately not included in that year's judicial reform package; Pride events and LGBTQ gatherings were repeatedly disallowed in 2024 and 2025 with police detaining participants, per Amnesty International. The page carries no Düzce-specific content, so it stands only as the framework against which the record's national-score-derived model estimate for Düzce sits.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's Turkey country overview independently corroborates and updates the national-framework claims in the Edirne record: same-sex activity has been decriminalised since the 1858 Ottoman penal code and transgender people could change legal gender from 1988, yet same-sex marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships remain unavailable with no comprehensive anti-discrimination law, while LGBTQ people are barred from open military service. Crucially for the record's October 2025 draft-law claim, Wikipedia reports that in early 2026 Turkish media said the government was considering legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex', but that provision was ultimately not included in that year's judicial reform package. It also dates the surrounding hostility: in May 2025 Erdoğan declared a 'Decade of Family and Population' for 2026-2035 at the International Family Forum with explicit anti-LGBTI rhetoric, Pride events were repeatedly disallowed in 2024 and 2025 with police detaining participants, and the European Commission's Türkiye Report 2025 concludes the country's laws and their implementation do not properly protect LGBTQ people. The page has nothing Edirne-specific, so it functions purely as the framework document under which a visitor to Edirne stands.
